title: You Feel Yourself Decide to Move, Yet Your Brain Starts 350 Milliseconds Earlier
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Benjamin Libet (1983): The -550 ms Readiness Potential, Conscious 'W-Time' & Schurger's Neural Noise Twist, grounded in Benjamin Libet, Curtis A. Gleason, Elwood W. Wright, Dennis K. Pearl (1983) (Brain). Empirical findings show that in 1983 at UC San Francisco, Benjamin Libet asked healthy volunteers to flick their right wrist spontaneously 'whenever the urge struck' while recording both forearm EMG muscle onset (0 ms) and vertex scalp EEG over supplementary motor / premotor cortex.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how premotor cortex, prefrontal cortex, motor cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that to timestamp the exact millisecond a participant first FELT the conscious urge to move ('W-time'), they watched a bright green cathode-ray oscilloscope spot revolving once every 2.56 seconds (nearly 25x faster than a wall second hand, ~43 ms per scale tick) and reported where the dot stood when the urge popped into awareness.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Benjamin Libet, Curtis A. Gleason, Elwood W. Wright, Dennis K. Pearl (1983). TIME OF CONSCIOUS INTENTION TO ACT IN RELATION TO ONSET OF CEREBRAL ACTIVITY (READINESS-POTENTIAL). Brain. https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/106.3.623
- Benjamin Libet (2000). Conscious and Unconscious Mental Activity: Commentary by Benjamin Libet (San Francisco). Neuropsychoanalysis. https://doi.org/10.1080/15294145.2000.10773277
- Benjamin Libet (1991). Conscious vs neural time. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/352027a0

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
